svg.title: A thoughtful message for Valentine’s Day

text.tspan: Everyday English - B1 - 2026/02/08 - Essay - 01
A handmade greeting creates a personal message.
Pexels · 6765938
A thoughtful message for Valentine’s Day
There is more than one way to send a thoughtful greeting. In my experience, practical preparation and attention to others are two
useful starting points.
One reason is that a specific message expresses care more clearly than a grand phrase. For instance, we thank a friend for a
particular act of kindness. This prevents a small difficulty from taking over the experience. It also leaves us more time to notice what
is happening.
Another reason is that respecting the recipient makes a greeting considerate. For example, we avoid assuming that everyone wants a
romantic message. This approach recognises that the experience belongs to more than one person and that different people may
need different things.
These examples show why preparation and consideration work well together. We do not have to control every detail. We can make a
sensible arrangement and remain ready to respond.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a clear main idea; develop two different points with examples; bring them together in the conclusion. Each
body paragraph needs a distinct point and a concrete example. The conclusion should connect the argument rather than introduce a
new proposal.
Persuade a group to change how they send a thoughtful greeting. Support your recommendation with two different reasons and a
practical example of each. Use four short paragraphs: introduction, two developed points, and conclusion. (Model: One possible
outline: introduce the situation; discuss a specific message expresses care more clearly than a grand phrase with an example;
discuss respecting the recipient makes a greeting considerate with a different example; conclude by connecting the two points.)
